answers.ask: No look was stated - military, sci-fi, or bright and arcade?
answers.answer: Use a military-themed battle arena with clear, practical cover and readable weapon designs.

answers.ask: How many players fight at once? A 2:30 free-for-all plays very differently at 6 players than at 20, and that sets the arena size.
answers.answer: Make it a 6-player free-for-all so the arena can stay compact and fast-paced.

scene_prompt: Create a compact, military-themed 3D battle arena for a 6-player free-for-all, with practical cover arranged to support fast movement. Build a clear central combat zone with low barriers, crates, and sightline breaks, surrounded by connected side lanes and elevated firing positions for varied assault-rifle, sniper, revolver, shotgun, and pistol engagements.
agent_notes: Shooter: guns, kills, respawns and a most-kills timer, with the author settling it as a compact 6-player free-for-all. Arena Deathmatch was the closest preset by mode, but a free-for-all has no team traffic to channel so its lane-network went, and its weapon and armour spawns contradict an economy where you own weapons out of coin-bought boxes, so with the shape swapped and most of the options gone I recorded it as built from scratch rather than claim the preset. space-bounded from the shared catalogue is the arena the prompt actually describes — one bounded single-level fighting space — and it keeps the build on P0; I kept path-loop because an arcade free-for-all wants interconnected routes rather than dead ends, and cover-los because the author asked for clear practical cover in a military arena. With no user to ask I assumed spawn-protected scattered respawn points rather than two mirrored bases, since players respawn continuously in a tight arena, and treated the coins, weapon boxes and 2:30 timer as economy and match rules that do not change the map.
